evals.name: no-idea-full-interview
evals.prompt: I need images for my bakery's new website but I honestly have no idea what they should look like
evals.expected_output: One batch of plain-language questions with recommendations and options; no shortlist or prompt yet unless the context already answers them.
expectations: All questions arrive in a single reply
It asks who sees the images or where they appear only if the ask leaves it open, and does not re-ask that it is a bakery website
It asks for the feeling in about three words and offers ready-made word sets to react to
It asks what the images must never look like
It asks whether the look should be photographic, drawn, 3D or flat graphic, with a recommendation
No image-generation prompt is written

evals.name: shortlist-contrasts-on-two-axes
evals.prompt: It's for a bakery website. The feeling is honest, warm, a bit playful. Never corporate or glossy. You choose the medium. Today, not retro. Shortlist some looks.
evals.expected_output: Three named directions with variants that differ on at least two axes, each with a reason tied to the user's words, a one-sentence picture, a risk, and a recommendation; offers the optional sketch round with its cost.
expectations: Exactly three directions are shortlisted, each named with a specific variant
The three differ in medium (not three photographic looks)
Each direction has a one-line reason that uses the user's words (honest, warm or playful)
Each direction names the way it could go wrong
One direction is recommended
A sketch round is offered as optional with its cost stated, and nothing is rendered
No direction is described as 'in the style of' a named artist, studio or photographer

evals.name: same-pose-goes-to-shots
evals.prompt: Every image I make of our founder comes out the same: straight on, centered, smiling at the camera. The look is fine, it's just boring. Help.
evals.expected_output: Treats the shot, not the style, as the problem and offers two or three contrasting shot options with what each communicates.
expectations: It does not propose a new style or ask the full style interview
It offers two or three shot options
The options differ on at least two of camera height, distance, subject placement and pose
None of the options is eye level, centered and facing the camera
Each option states what it communicates
Pose and gaze are described as body mechanics or direction (for example 'looking camera-right, out of frame'), not adjectives alone

evals.name: named-umbrella-style-asks-variant
evals.expected_output: Treats 'retro' as an umbrella and asks which strand, offering concrete decade variants.
expectations: It says 'retro' covers several different looks
It offers at least three decade-specific variants (for example 50s atomic, 70s warm, 80s synthwave, 90s grunge)
Each variant is described concretely by palette, medium or type
It recommends one variant or asks a question that decides between them

evals.name: living-artist-becomes-attributes
evals.prompt: I want it to look exactly like a living illustrator I love — I'll give you their name — for our product poster.
evals.expected_output: Declines to use the artist's name and instead asks for or describes the attributes that make the work appealing.
expectations: It explains that a direction is not written as 'in the style of' a living artist
It offers to capture the look through attributes such as line, palette, texture and composition
It asks which properties of the work the user likes, or maps them to library directions
No style block or prompt contains an artist's name

evals.name: readback-and-docs-precedence
evals.prompt: Go with Analog film, warm consumer color, shot option B. Our docs/brand.md says dark editorial look, 1600x900 heroes, headline over the right 40%.
evals.expected_output: A readback block where the direction rules the look and the docs supply only size and text zone, plus a style block and a one-time save offer.
expectations: The readback keeps the 1600x900 size and the right-40% headline zone from the docs
The docs' dark editorial look is mentioned once as replaced, not blended in and not asked about repeatedly
Palette, light, texture, shot and composition lines are concrete (no bare 'moody' or 'well lit')
Light is stated with direction and a color temperature or shadow share
The subject placement keeps the right 40% clear for the headline
A style block in full sentences is included, with exclusions phrased as positive states
It offers once to save the look to docs/art-direction.md and writes nothing without a yes

evals.name: series-rotates-shots
evals.prompt: We need five LinkedIn images for a series about our engineers, documentary candid look. Plan the shots.
evals.expected_output: Keeps one direction and assigns different shot recipes across the five images.
expectations: The direction stays Documentary / candid for all five
At least four different shot recipes are used across the five images
At least one image uses an unusual height (overhead, ground-level or high-angle)
No image has the subject looking into the lens unless that is stated as deliberate
Composition for each image names where the subject sits in the frame

evals.name: staging-physics-sheet
evals.prompt: Analog film, warm consumer color, shot A (candid mid-action) is locked. It's a 1600x900 hero for our bakery site, headline top-right. Now plan the actual scene so it doesn't look fake — people should notice the bread first.
evals.expected_output: A scene sheet for shot A: every object with a role and a real size, the camera placed physically with the frame shares that follow, light reasoned into shadow direction and length, contact and materials, and a ranked emphasis plan in which the bread wins.
expectations: Every object in frame is listed, including the surface it stands on and the background surface
Exactly one hero is named, and it is the bread
Each object has a real-world size (cm or m)
Camera height, distance to the hero and lens feel are stated, and the hero's frame share is consistent with its size and that distance
Each light source is given a direction and an elevation or height, and the shadow direction (and length or edge hardness) follows from it
Contact with the supporting surface is stated (a contact shadow or what the object rests on)
Which objects are sharp and which are soft is stated, consistent with the stated distances
Emphasis is given as an order (first, second, third read) with a specific detail on the hero, and at least one competitor (a face, a window, a bright surface) is named with how it is held down
The headline zone top-right is filled by a named physical surface kept low in contrast
Nothing is described 'in the style of' a named artist or photographer
It does not ask the user for distances, camera height, angles or aperture; it decides them and states them on the sheet

evals.name: fake-looking-goes-to-staging
evals.prompt: My generated product shots of our perfume bottle look fake. The bottle kind of floats, the reflections look weird, and the background steals attention. The look itself is fine.
evals.expected_output: Treats staging, not style, as the problem: reasons out support and contact, glass physics and reflections, light geometry and emphasis, and asks only for what it cannot know, such as the bottle's real size.
expectations: It does not shortlist new directions or run the style interview
It names the missing contact (a contact shadow or the surface the bottle rests on) as the cause of floating
It reasons about glass physically: refraction of what is behind the bottle, and highlights or reflections placed on the side of the stated light source
It states the light sources with their directions instead of a mood word
It gives an emphasis plan in which the bottle or a named detail of it wins, and says how the background is held down (focus, value, saturation or distance)
It asks for the bottle's real dimensions or states an assumed size
Physics is written for the prompt as visible results (relations, frame shares, shadow directions), not only as centimeters
It does not ask the user for distances, camera height or angles
